title: Énorme potentiel mais ...
body:
J'espère que cette application continuera de se développer, car elle possède de nombreuses forces. Par contre, actuellement je ne suis pas prêt à débourser pour l'abonnement annuel pour les raisons suivantes: 

La synchronisation se fait à sens unique (importation de calendrier seulement). On doit donc utiliser 2 type d'applications pour arriver à nos buts.

Les couleurs associées au types d'événement enregistrés constituent la force de cet outil. Cependant, Toutes les couleurs se ressemblent et ont peu de contraste entre elles. De plus La synchronisation des couleurs des différents  calendriers semble buggée (elles apparaissent aléatoirement, lorsqu'on touche l'évènement).

L'aspect visuel est à revoir. L'œil est rapidement surchargé, surtout en mode pleine page: les heures et titres d'un événement sont répétés à chaque intervalle, en plus des zones rayées, des petits carreaux et ont peine à distinguer les journées. 

Quelques fonctions à mon avis essentielle à bonifier : l'espace pour prendre des notes sur un événement est pertinent, mais il est difficile à consulter et parfois il ne s'ouvre pas au touché. 

Je n'ai pas su comment déplacer plusieurs cases du même événement (rare sont les événement uniquement de  15 minutes). Il serait pertinent de les déplacer en bloc, car les rendez-vous changent régulièrement et on doit le repérer pour chaque intervalle. 

Ce sont ces choses qui rendent ce type d'outil actuellement inefficace pour moi et ce malgré ses puissantes fonctions: créer des listes de tache récurrentes, associer des couleurs, synchroniser à des application de tâches et bien plus. Si les mises à jour venaient à corriger les problèmes mentionnés, je m'abonnerais à vie. Bonne chance.

I would definitely recommend trying this App if you are into Time Blocking. Another plus is the Developer is very active , listens to comments and is bringing new updates
Updated 11th Jan 2022
The latest update has added a number of additional features which raise this app to a new level. A couple of them are : You can import all the appointments from your diary with it working seamlessly in the background : A new Week view has been introduced which gives the opportunity to plan ahead . Well done to the developer who listens to what the users say.

The latest update has made an already outstanding app even better. The enhanced notification system, calendar sync, and new recurrence patterns show the developer's commitment to continuous improvement.

The responsive customer service is the cherry on top - it's clear the developer truly cares about user experience and feedback.

title: The app that fulfilled my 25-year search
body: This app provides everything I need on a daily basis to map out how to spend my time. When I was a very-young-adult, I found that a strict time schedule worked very well for me to work consistently toward my goals, but life is much more complicated now and I need something that provides flexibility along with structure. The functionality in this app is amazing - customizable to my heart’s desire - and incredibly fun and satisfactory to use. Every day I look forward to using it to help me stay on point and be able to pivot on a moment’s notice. It is especially helpful when I have to budget for a specific window of time so that I can realistically plan what I can achieve by a specific deadline. The color coding (including abundant color palettes to choose from) and ability to set color “rules” (so that any key word I program automatically turns the color I want) gives the app another layer or dimension for staying organized. The ability to drag and drop, copy and paste, and expand, shrink, and lock time blocks provides the flexibility that my middle-aged life requires, while still giving me the type of solid plan that worked for me decades ago. With options to view time at different scales (single day, 3-day, week, and month), and with multiple ways to enter information onto the calendar and multiple ways to make changes, this app can accommodate anyone’s needs and preferences. The bulk import feature makes it an absolute breeze to migrate your to-do lists to this app. This is the single best useful app I have ever paid for, and I can’t imagine my life without it now. So thankful for Luke and all his hard work! He is constantly striving to make this app better, and every update makes that evident.

title: Lifesaver. Helps me get 2-3x done in a day
body:
This is my favorite app, I use it every hour of the day. Time blocking is the one thing that helps me go from getting nothing done to having a productive day, but keeping track of things on paper/notes/calendar all have their issues. I’ve used Todoist, TickTick, and tested a few others at the same time as TimeFinder before seeing it was exactly what I needed. TimeFinder makes it SO SO quick to jot down tasks, assign task durations and add them to your day’s schedule. I jot down every little thing so I never forget to do anything, and it shows me how quickly little things add up. It lets me see how realistic my day looks - often my task list for the day is 12hr+ so I know I need to redistribute. And the schedule keeps me on track so that I just power through all my tasks, and keeps me mindful of what tasks I can or cannot get done in between appointments etc. Having everything on a schedule with time estimates keeps you realistic but also efficient - commute, gym, lunch, dinner, etc all mean you have less time in the day than you think but also seeing windows of spare time allows you to schedule a lot of small nagging things to check off in between. And when things come up it’s sooo much easier to move things around on TimeFinder than it is on paper or a calendar.

Luke, the developer, is incredibly responsive and is always quick to fix bugs and open to feedback. I’ve suggested a couple features that were there the next day. That’s one of the reasons I love it so much - the design is in our hands as the user and I trust that it will only get better.

Love this app, highly recommend

title: This is how you save your day.
body:
Ok, here is the thing, if you use this app, you will truly get your tasks done and reclaim your day. 

If you just download the app, you will not. 

It’s important to make timefinder a part of your morning, and it is also important to use your reminders app (or some other task app) to get your tasks in there. 

The magic of time finder is that you have to think about how long something is going to take you, and then you will feel like to have to accomplish it. 

I have pretty bad ADHD, and this helps keep the pressure on. Otherwise I do deep dives into bacteria found in rabbits ears or how many cargo ships have sunk in the last 50 years.

It is 100% worth it to spend 10 minutes at the start of your day, or the end of the previous day to plan out your day.

Plan in SOME free time, so that you can have a place where you just handle immediate ’emergency’ stuff. Maybe 1 hour in the morning and 1 hour at afternoon. 

I plan in my morning exercises, rest, meals. The app will move you along. But you get a real feeling of accomplishment.

📅 This app allows you to take control of your schedule. Other apps may boast of this, but in my experience, none are as simple or as user-friendly as this one.

🧠 What most impresses me about this app is its ability to manage my mind.  (Am I the only one who can relate to that meme about my mind being like an internet browser with 19 tabs open, 3 that are frozen, and no idea where the music is coming from?)

Thanks to TimeFinder, I can make quick work of scheduling my day (I have a list of routines saved for frequent tasks: get ready for work, commute, work, lunch break) while also making sure my To-Do lists get gone. The widget and Apple Watch notifications keep my on track throughout the day.

You know that awful feeling when you’re trying to go to sleep, but get flooded with a long list of things you need to do?  I even have a specific list dedicated to that. It’s not in a random place to be forgotten about, but it’s in TimeFinder where I can easily drag and drop it to my schedule as time allows and then mark it done— and I don’t mean figuratively.  A feature within TimeFinder allows you to mark tasks as done from within a list and as you complete it on the schedule. 

One word of caution: Because this app is so intuitive, you may think it a waste of time to view the video tutorial in the settings. You can easily navigate the app and get great benefit from it even if you don’t, but if you do watch it, you’ll get the scoop on some other great time-saving features that will maximize the overall benefit of the app.

If you really want to save yourself some time, you’ll stop reading reviews and download it to see for yourself!

title: 5-Star App: Transparency Is Key
body:

From the outside looking in, it looks like a lot of false promises. However, I do believe the dev’s claim that he prioritizing shipping fully-fleshed updates.

 However, I’ve revised my previous rating for two reasons: 

1. I didn’t reach out to the dev privately about any issues I had on the timeline of things, though I have reached out previously about a separate issue and he was responsive. I typically do that, but failed to in this case. That’s on me.

2. TimeFinder’s current app is still worthy of five stars. Reviews aren’t meant to be places to air out grievances against a dev for a problem you’ve never mentioned before, they’re to let other users know whether an app is worth it. I believe TimeFinder is. 

Keeping the below for posterity, and a little humility on my end. I was wrong to handle my issue this way, and I’m glad the dev was relatively nice about it.

OLD Review:

I have watched this dev promise significant updates for nearly two years now. I am genuinely excited for the next iteration of TimeFinder, but this guy is constantly saying it’s near or coming soon or in the next few weeks (last update, nearly three months ago 😂). You have a genuinely good app that people enjoy using, just remove those update notes that you can’t or haven’t delivered (which is fine!!!!) from each update. Seriously, I’m coming to you person-to-person, re-read the new features and updates you’ve failed to deliver on for years, promises which users wouldn’t even be aware of if you didn’t keep advertising it! Also, I’ve already paid for lifetime, you already have my money, so take your time. But just stop mentioning timelines and missing them for Pete’s sake! Just disappointed.

This is fine and easy enough, but what I can’t do is drag them from schedule view into list view in TimeFinder. If I can drag and drop one way, I should be able to drag and drop the other way, otherwise I have to retype everything into list view and delete from the schedule in order to maintain an untimed list like on my calendar app. 

Also in TimeFinder you can’t have more than one list item at the same time, so those need to be adjusted as well or when TimeFinder imports them it will group them all into one line of text that you will need to manually edit. 

These are really just nitpicking type things though, I’m not sure what implementing them would entail and overall I like the app and believe that it will prove to be useful.

I love how you can colour code things and set the time blocks to be 5, 10, 15, 30, or 60 minutes. The lists are also good. I use them to keep track of what homework I need to do, and then I can cross it out! It’s also good for grocery lists and such. Repeating tasks, of course, are super useful. I also think that it’s super easy to move tasks around and add new ones. The whole app is really easy to navigate and use and looks great! I would definitely recommend it to everyone! 

Even though this app is AMAZING, there are a few thing that I think would make it even better. First, notifications. I would like if you could set up notifications to remind me about specific tasks for like 1 or 5 or 10 minutes before a task. This would help me stay on track. I know there are already notifications for tasks at the time they start but I think having notifications before tasks would also be helpful. Next, I would really like a section where you could set reminders and keep track of events that you couldn’t put on a daily schedule since they’re all day things, like birthdays, holidays, first day of school/work, etc. I would also love if there was a notes section where you could just add notes with random information you need to jot down or even a sort of journal (it would also be great if you could type and use an Apple Pencil to hand write). I also think it would be great to have more options for recurring tasks. I love the option right now of choosing which day(s) to repeat tasks, but I would also love if you could repeats tasks on, say, Saturday every two weeks, or every month. 

Sorry for the super long review! I really love this app and it’s so great! The things I think would make it better are obviously just suggestions but I hope you consider them! Thanks for an amazing app that really makes me so much more productive!

 EDIT: the developer is very responsive and helpful! I sent an email and the response was very timely and helpful!

title: Reduced my stress
body:
love this app for keeping my sanity of which tasks to focus on and which to do another day.  This app allows me to brain dump all my tasks into a list and then decide each day which ones to slide into my schedule. I can make todo lists for each work project and not have to write them on a separate calendar. In the paid version, it also syncs to your external calendar events by automatically blocking  them in for you. 

It’s reduced my stress because I frequently over fill my day from imagining I can do more.  Now I can realistically know what I can do for that day by visually seeing a concrete plan of blocked tasks.  It’s so much better than just a list of tasks written into a calendar to fit in around meetings.

And if I don’t finish a task that day, it’s easy to add it back into my schedule the next day. I can also see my progress on which tasks I’ve completed. So I can easily count up the hours spent on each project. 

I have a hard time estimating how long tasks take and by extending  the time block and moving a task to the next day, I’ve been realizing how much I under estimate my time projections. No wonder I always feel behind. 

It’s so easy to extend the time block for a task and move other tasks to a different time block. You can set up time blocks as small as 5 minutes. And you can drag over multiple tasks into one time block. 

I also want to add that the user interface is so simple and intuitive to use. It’s great not to feel overwhelmed by features. It also syncs across all Mac devices for the paid version. And there are notifications for each time block. You can test out so many features in the free version. I paid for the premium version to sync my calendar and use over all my devices. The developer also takes feedback of feature requests and improves the app with them. 

I feel in command of my work schedule now. Having ADHD and difficulty with time management and with trouble getting started on tasks because my todo list seems overwhelming, it’s been a life saver for me.
author: LynnProgrammer

title: Useful tool that is also flexible!
body:
I really love this app. I feel like app works hand in hand with the tools that productivity experts suggest in order to be more organized. Time blocking is an excellent way to organize your day. 

I have been using the Premium version of the app for a few months now, and I’ll list the pros and cons:

-Pros
1. Flexibility. I love the click and drop feature where you can just grab and change a time block if your schedule changes. Additionally, being able to extend a time block (for extra time), has allowed me to get a better grasp on how long I take to carry out tasks. 

2. Multiple views (incl. Split View and week view). These views are excellent. It’s easy to go back and forth between them and get an overview of two consecutive days or be able to see the week as a whole. 

3. High level of personalization. You can pick the colors you want to use, the time intervals (for instance, if you prefer to have a schedule divided up by 30 minute intervals instead of hourly). You can also pick what time your day begins and ends so you aren’t having to schedule hours you would usually be asleep. It gives for nice visibility. 

4. Calendar Sync. This feature has been so nice because you can link the app up with your calendars to automatically add whatever events you have going on, then you know those times are blocked already. 

5. Lists. I use my lists in a variety of ways. Some of them are dedicated for specific days while others I have made into categories, such as ‘chores’ that I know I frequently carry out but I might not have a set date or time I do them each week. 

6. Luke (the app’s developer). This was the first app I’ve ever really felt genuinely invested in. I wanted to give feedback on how to improve the app, but also share how much the app has helped me. Luke is very approachable and proactive (as well as being kind)!  He’s actually invested in this app and cares about user feedback. I had requested for the days of the week to be added to the dates, and that was something that was released with an update! 😄🥰 

-Con:

1. The icons. The only thing that is a con are the lack of variety when it comes to icons when making lists, but honestly, this is so minor, I wasn’t even sure I wanted to include this….but felt like I still wanted this to be an honest review. 

That’s the only con because I can see how much of a leap the app has taken since I began using it. The last update offered so many great features…features I hadn’t even thought of, that were really useful and definitely improved the overall quality of the app. 

————————————————————————-
Conclusion:

Overall, I really like this app. It helps me stay organized while still allowing some flexibility because….life happens and plans change! This app really keeps up with me and my strange freelancing schedule. 

The approachability of the apps developer is also a huge plus. 

I would recommend to all my friends and family!!

title: Almost but not quite.
body:
I like a lot about this app. It’s a pretty good planner. But there are some distinct flaws. So, what I wanted it to do that it doesn’t do was noticeably notifying me to move on to the next task. The little click noises are insufficiently different from the sound my keyboard makes to be noticeable or loud enough or distinctive enough to draw my attention in the ambient noise of the lab. The banner notifications outside the app aren’t bad IF I’m looking at my phone, but if I am concentrating obviously I don’t see them. This could cause me to miss the timing on things. Also the inability to change the time divisions of the schedule without erasing everything is no good. Somethings take 10 minutes other things need hours. This flaw that erases the whole thing when I change the time increments essentially means that I have to leave it on five minute increments -all the time- because I need the finest time resolution -sometimes- and that’s a real design flaw. The third thing that would be a nice feature (not essential, but really nice) is a way to look at the day and week as a graph or an icon. So like for a day you would put a image of a clock and show maybe even using the colors that we use inside the planner a blocked out clock showing us visually our planned day we could see when we have free time to block for other things rather than all the scrolling. Also for like a week to see when we can stick that “meeting that really should’ve been an email“ in a day that we can identify that -I got free time on Thursday next week to have this useless meeting- And finally I have to say that it’s not easy to navigate when you plan things pretty far in advance. Scheduling for next week isn’t too bad but if I want to schedule for next month or two months from now it’s a lot of clicking to go to that date. 

So to reiterate my recommendations: 

1: A louder noticeable notification option. 

2: the ability to retain the schedule when changing time increments. 

3: some single screen graphic visualization of a day’s time blocks. (And a weeks if possible) 

4: a easier mechanism to navigate the calendar to weeks or months far in advance. 

I keep looking for a planner app that really delivers all the features I’m asking for and this one’s pretty good, but some of the things it’s missing to me seems really tragic because it has the potential to be a perfect app and I’m looking for something that allows me to delete the zillions of alarms I have to have and the other planner and calendar apps that do partial jobs of what I’m looking for. Because frankly having to use five apps plus all the alarms on my clock to keep the schedule together is a waste of my time and the whole purpose of these apps is to recover as much of my time for myself and for my efficiency as possible. that being said I understand programming apps is a lot of work and so really thank you for trying to deliver the product it’s just not quite effective enough for me yet. Implement a few more features and it really will be great.
